checks.name: Shell acquires a renewable lease before requesting SDK or service remotes
a failed initial lease never boots service remotes
live renewals extend protection and stale cleanup requests cannot override new responses
short network loss preserves input and recovery renews the same tab
an expired offline tab cannot interact, fetch, load another remote or execute a cached factory
real browser freeze and resume validates the server lease before further use
expiry is irreversible but still protects files until explicit cleanup after the grace period
legacy unknown tabs cannot be classified as protected or released by timeout
cleanup enforces confirmation and same-origin controls
UI releases only the expired tab and keeps its tombstone and a new retention period
active tabs and rollback references still prevent deletion after stale-tab cleanup
late heartbeat and open requests cannot revive released records or enter a retired composition
only after other references clear and post-cleanup retention passes are files actually deleted
the returning stale browser stays blocked and its explicit reload opens the latest composition
released evidence survives restart and remains reviewable on mobile
original service files and the live repository remain unchanged

scope: Real browser/API in a disposable store: lease renewal, offline and frozen resume gates, explicit stale session release, deletion guards and actual removal. Browser clocks and past metadata simulate elapsed time; production has no clock override.
